# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall (clip-on): Bose Ultra Open Earbuds, about $199 (list $299)**
- Runner's World picks it as best overall. It praises the sound, comfort, and easy controls, and says the buds don't bounce.
- WIRED likes the physical buttons for use while running.
- Downsides: only IPX4 water resistance, about 7 hours per charge, and it's pricey.
- Runner's World says Bose is releasing new open-ear earbuds within a month, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts on these.
- [Runner's World guide with buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)

**Best for long runs and rain: Shokz OpenDots 2, $200**
- WIRED's top pick: 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. The reviewer wore them in rain and submerged them without problems.
- The top of the ear stays free for glasses or hats.
- [WIRED's best open earbuds](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, $180 list (listed around $125 at some retailers)**
- Bone conduction gives you the most awareness of traffic. It has physical buttons, 12 hours of battery, and IP55 rating.
- WIRED rated it 8/10 for fit and big sound, but noted the clarity isn't quite as good as the previous OpenRun's.
- Runner's World notes the neckband can interfere with long hair, low ponytails, and winter hats.
- [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

**Best value hook-style: Soundcore AeroFit 2**
- SoundGuys calls it the best budget pick and lists it at $79.99 on Amazon. It has IP55 protection and long battery life.
- Dealectric lists 10 hours per bud, 42 hours with the case, and wireless charging. It shows a $129.99 store price and $104 with code AFSC20. That's quite different from SoundGuys' price, so compare before buying.
- [Buy at Soundcore's US store via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). It's an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Use code AFSC20 at checkout, and the store's checkout price is final.
- [SoundGuys' open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**Cheapest way to try the concept:**
- The JLab Flex Open (about $40–50) is Runner's World's budget pick. Sound is less detailed, and the controls are touch-only. [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/)
- The Soundpeats PearlClip Pro (about $50) is WIRED's cheap pick. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

**Also worth a look:** SoundGuys names the Nothing Ear (Open) best for running, at about $99 on Amazon (list $149) with an IP54 rating. [SoundGuys' workout earbuds guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

## Quick pick
- **Want the best sound and comfort:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Run in all weather or do long runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Want maximum awareness of traffic:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Watching your budget:** Soundcore AeroFit 2 or a ~$50 clip-on.

Open-ear buds let in outside sound but don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear what's around you.
